title: 人人都有價碼
imageAlt: A thoughtful person stands beside a large price tag and coins, illustrating the proverb's cynical metaphor.
imageAltZh: 一個人站在大型價錢牌和硬幣旁，呈現這句諺語的悲觀比喻。
imageCaption: The imaginary price tag represents the cynical claim that enough money or benefit can buy a person's loyalty or principles.
imageCaptionZh: 想像中的價錢牌代表一種悲觀看法：足夠的金錢或利益可以收買一個人的忠誠或原則。

examples.en: The businessman believed that every man has his price.
examples.zh: 那名商人相信人人都有價碼。

meaning.en: This proverb expresses the cynical belief that every person can eventually be persuaded to act dishonestly, abandon a principle or betray somebody if the money or personal benefit offered is great enough.
meaning.zh: 這句諺語以悲觀甚至犬儒的方式表示：只要有人提出足夠多的金錢、利益或其他好處，任何人最終都可能被說服做出不誠實的行為、放棄原則或背叛他人。
naturalZh: 只要利益夠大，任何人都可能動搖
人的忠誠或原則可以被收買
沒有人完全不受金錢或利益誘惑
任何人都有可能為利益妥協
meaning.tendencyEn: Price is figurative: it means the money or benefit supposedly needed to buy a person's honesty, loyalty or principles. The saying is a cynical generalisation, not an established fact.
meaning.tendencyZh: price 在這裏是比喻用法，指據說要付出多少金錢或利益，才可以「買下」一個人的誠信、忠誠或原則。這句話是悲觀的概括，而不是已證實的事實。

modelExample.sourceEn: The businessman believed that anyone could be persuaded to betray their principles if enough money was offered.
modelExample.sourceZh: 那名商人認為，只要出價夠高，任何人都可能被說服背棄原則。
modelExample.answerEn: The businessman believed that every man has his price.
modelExample.answerZh: 那名商人相信人人都有價碼。
modelExample.compressedEn: Anybody may abandon their principles if enough money is offered.
modelExample.compressedZh: 只要出價夠高，任何人都可能放棄原則。

register.labelZh: 句法中性；語氣強烈悲觀及犬儒
register.summaryEn: The grammar is neutral, but the meaning is strongly cynical and distrustful. Saying it directly about a particular person may be insulting because it suggests that the person has no firm principles.
register.summaryZh: 這個表達的句法本身屬中性，但意思帶有強烈的悲觀、不信任及犬儒色彩。直接用來形容某一個人可能令人感到受冒犯，因為它暗示對方沒有堅定原則。
contextsZh: 有關誠信及忠誠的辯論

tones.en: The speaker presents human loyalty as something that money or personal benefit can buy.
tones.zh: 說話者把人的忠誠描述成可以被金錢或個人利益收買的東西。

tones.en: The speaker may report a character's pessimistic view without personally agreeing with it.
tones.zh: 說話者可以轉述某個人物的悲觀看法，而不表示自己認同。

tones.en: The proverb can be quoted in order to challenge the idea that everybody can be bought.
tones.zh: 說話者可以引用這句諺語，質疑「所有人都可以被收買」的想法。

sensitiveContextsEn: direct accusations about a particular person's honesty
serious allegations of bribery or corruption
situations where traditional gendered wording may distract or offend
sensitiveContextsZh: 直接質疑某一個人的誠信
嚴重的賄賂或貪污指控
傳統性別用語可能令人分心或不適的情況
register.sensitivityEn: The traditional words man and his once referred to people in general, but they are now gendered and may sound old-fashioned. Gender-neutral alternatives include everyone has a price and everyone can be bought; this exercise nevertheless practises the exact traditional proverb.
register.sensitivityZh: 傳統上，man 和 his 可以泛指所有人，但現代英語中這兩個字帶有性別色彩，也可能顯得較古老。較中性的說法包括 everyone has a price 和 everyone can be bought；本練習仍會練習指定的傳統諺語。
register.formalEn: Use the proverb only when its cynical attitude genuinely suits the context. A plain, evidence-based explanation is usually safer in highly formal or sensitive writing.
register.formalZh: 只有當這句諺語的悲觀語氣確實符合語境時才應使用。在高度正式或敏感的文字中，直接而有證據的說明通常更加穩妥。

fixedVariable.fixedEn: The five words remain fixed and must appear in this order.
fixedVariable.fixedZh: 這五個字及其排列次序不可改變。

capitalisation.en: Capitalise the first word when the proverb begins a sentence.
capitalisation.zh: 諺語放在句首時，第一個字母使用大寫。

capitalisation.example: He believes that every man has his price.
capitalisation.en: Use lower case when the proverb sits inside a longer sentence.
capitalisation.zh: 諺語放在較長句子中時，通常使用小寫。

fixedVariable.variableEn: The proverb itself normally remains unchanged. The reporting frame, speaker position, tense and certainty around it may vary.
fixedVariable.variableZh: 諺語本身通常保持不變；可以改變的是外圍的轉述框架、說話者立場、時態及確定程度。
variableItemsEn: the tense of the reporting verb

forms.example: He believes that every man has his price.
He believed that every man has his price.
forms.exampleZh: 他當時相信人人都有價碼。

forms.example: He has always believed that every man has his price.
forms.exampleZh: 他一直相信人人都有價碼。

forms.example: He will argue that every man has his price.
forms.exampleZh: 他將會主張人人都有價碼。

forms.example: Does Marcus really believe that every man has his price?
forms.exampleZh: Marcus 真的相信人人都有價碼嗎？

forms.example: “Every man has his price,” the dealer said.
forms.exampleZh: 那名商人說：「人人都有價碼。」

forms.example: She rejects the idea that every man has his price.
forms.exampleZh: 她反駁「人人都有價碼」這個想法。

specificForms.descriptionEn: Use the proverb as a complete statement when the cynical belief is already clear.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 當這種悲觀信念已經清楚時，可以把諺語當作完整陳述。

specificForms.formula: Subject + believe / think / say / claim + that + every man has his price.
specificForms.descriptionEn: Use a reporting verb to attribute the cynical belief to another person or character.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 使用轉述動詞，把這種悲觀看法歸於另一個人或角色。

examples.en: The businessman believed that every man has his price.
examples.zh: 那名商人相信人人都有價碼。

notes.en: Has may remain in the present simple after a past reporting verb because the proverb states a general belief.
notes.zh: 即使轉述動詞使用過去式，諺語中的 has 仍可保留現在式，因為它表達一般信念。

specificForms.titleEn: Describing the Belief as an Idea
specificForms.formula: Subject + present / express / hold + the belief that + every man has his price.
specificForms.descriptionEn: Name the proverb as a belief rather than presenting it as fact.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 把諺語明確稱為一種信念，而不是把它說成事實。

examples.en: The film presents the belief that every man has his price.
examples.zh: 這齣電影提出「人人都有價碼」這個信念。

specificForms.formula: Subject + question / challenge / reject + the idea that + every man has his price.
specificForms.descriptionEn: Use this frame when the source questions or rejects the proverb.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 原句質疑或反駁這句諺語時，使用這個框架。

examples.en: Her refusal challenges the idea that every man has his price.
examples.zh: 她的拒絕質疑了「人人都有價碼」這個想法。

specificForms.formula: Does + subject + believe that + every man has his price?
specificForms.descriptionEn: Ask whether somebody genuinely accepts the cynical belief.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 詢問某人是否真的認同這種悲觀看法。

examples.en: Does Marcus really believe that every man has his price?
examples.zh: Marcus 真的相信人人都有價碼嗎？

specificForms.formula: “Every man has his price,” + subject + said.
specificForms.descriptionEn: Quote the proverb directly and identify the speaker.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 直接引用整句諺語，並指出說話者。

examples.en: “Every man has his price,” the dealer said.
examples.zh: 那名商人說：「人人都有價碼。」

specificForms.formula: Although / Because / If + subject + believes that every man has his price, ...
specificForms.descriptionEn: Connect the reported belief to contrasting evidence, a reason or a condition.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 把被轉述的信念連接到相反證據、原因或條件。

examples.en: Although the director believes that every man has his price, the worker refuses every offer.
examples.zh: 雖然主管相信人人都有價碼，但員工拒絕了所有提議。

benefits.en: The proverb compresses the idea that anybody may abandon their principles if enough money is offered.
benefits.zh: 這句諺語把「只要金額足夠，任何人最終都可能放棄原則」這個較長概念濃縮成容易記憶的表達。

examples.en: He believes that every man has his price.

benefits.en: The expression reveals a pessimistic and distrustful view of human honesty.
benefits.zh: 這個表達顯示說話者對人的誠信抱有悲觀和不信任的態度。

benefits.en: It is useful when analysing a villain or dishonest character who believes that loyalty and principles can be bought.
benefits.zh: 分析反派、不誠實商人或其他相信忠誠和原則可以被收買的角色時，這句話十分有用。

benefits.titleEn: It Can Be Accepted, Questioned or Rejected
benefits.en: Different grammatical frames let the speaker report, question or reject the belief.
benefits.zh: 不同的句法框架讓學生可以轉述、質疑或反駁這個信念。

examples.en: Do you believe that every man has his price?
examples.zh: 你相信人人都有價碼嗎？

examples.en: She rejects the idea that every man has his price.
examples.zh: 她反駁「人人都有價碼」這個想法。

benefits.en: Students may encounter the proverb in films, crime stories, political commentary and discussions about corruption or loyalty.
benefits.zh: 學生可能會在電影、犯罪故事、政治評論，以及有關貪污或忠誠的討論中遇到這句諺語。

origin.statusEn: Early Record Well Documented; Exact Origin Unknown
origin.statusZh: 早期記錄有較充分證據；確切起源不明

history.en: One early documented form appeared in 1734 in connection with a speech by William Wyndham. It was described as an old maxim, suggesting that the saying was already known. The proverb is often attributed to Robert Walpole, but a later account records his narrower comment, “All those men have their price,” about a particular group of politicians; the broader proverb should not be presented as his proven invention.
history.zh: 其中一個較早而有記錄的版本在 1734 年出現，與 William Wyndham 的一篇演說有關。講者稱它為一句「古老格言」，顯示當時很可能已經流傳。這句諺語經常被歸於 Robert Walpole，但較後期記錄所載的是他針對一群特定政治人物所說的「那些人都有價碼」；因此不應把較廣泛的諺語說成肯定由他創造。

history.en: The ordinary word price refers to the money required to buy something. The proverb extends that idea metaphorically to human behaviour: money or personal advantage is imagined as buying cooperation, silence or betrayal.
history.zh: price 一般指購買物件所需的金額。這句諺語把概念比喻性地延伸至人的行為：金錢或個人利益被想像成可以購買一個人的合作、沉默或背叛。

history.en: Today, the expression remains a deliberately cynical claim that no person's honesty or loyalty is completely beyond temptation. It may also be quoted in order to question or reject that belief.
history.zh: 今天，這個表達仍然是一種刻意悲觀的說法，聲稱沒有人的誠信或忠誠能完全不受誘惑；說話者也可以引用它來質疑或反駁這種看法。

origin.memoryEn: A price tag suggests that something can be bought. The proverb cynically places an imaginary price tag on a person's principles.
origin.memoryZh: 價錢牌代表某件東西可以被購買。這句諺語悲觀地把一個想像中的價錢牌掛在人的原則之上。

rules.en: Every answer must contain the exact five-word proverb in the correct order.
rules.zh: 每個答案都必須準確包含五個字的目標諺語，不可更換或調動任何部分。

rules.en: The expression concerns supposedly buying a person's honesty, loyalty or principles, not the selling price of a product.
rules.zh: 這個表達指據說可以收買一個人的誠信、忠誠或原則，而不是貨品的售價。

examples.en: The criminal believes that every man has his price.
examples.zh: 那名罪犯相信人人都有價碼。

rules.titleEn: Use It for Bribery or Moral Compromise
rules.en: Use it when money or another benefit may cause dishonesty, betrayal, disclosure of a secret, disregard of a rule or abandonment of a moral principle.
rules.zh: 金錢或利益可能令人不誠實、背叛他人、洩露秘密、忽視規則或放棄道德原則時，才適合使用。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Use It for Normal Payment
rules.en: Receiving a salary, charging a fair price or accepting ordinary payment does not normally mean that somebody has been bought.
rules.zh: 收取薪金、訂立合理價錢或接受正常報酬，通常不代表某人被收買。

examples.en: The chef agreed to work for a monthly salary.

rules.en: Do not turn a source that questions, reports or rejects the proverb into a statement of fact.
rules.zh: 不可把質疑、轉述或反駁這句諺語的原句，改成確定事實。

examples.en: The film asks whether every man has his price.
examples.zh: 電影提出疑問：是否人人都有價碼。

rules.en: Words such as seems, suggests, may and believes show that the statement is an opinion rather than a proven fact.
rules.zh: seems、suggests、may 和 believes 等字詞表示這只是一個觀點，而不是已證實的事實。

rules.titleEn: Use the Gendered Traditional Form Carefully
rules.titleZh: 小心使用傳統性別用語
rules.en: The traditional proverb uses man and his but intends to include people of any gender. A gender-neutral alternative may be more appropriate outside this exact-form exercise.
rules.zh: 傳統諺語使用 man 和 his，但原意泛指任何性別的人。在本練習以外，較中性的說法有時會更合適。

rules.titleEn: The Proverb Does Not Approve of Bribery
rules.titleZh: 這句諺語並不表示贊成賄賂
rules.en: A speaker may quote the proverb in order to criticise, question or reject its cynical belief.
rules.zh: 說話者可以引用這句諺語來批評、質疑或反駁其中的犬儒看法。

instructions.en: Rewrite or respond to each item using every man has his price. Type the whole sentence; the first word of the model answer is provided.
instructions.zh: 使用 every man has his price 改寫句子或完成回應。請輸入完整句子；每題已提供參考答案的第一個字。

questions.prompt: The businessman believed that anyone could be persuaded to act dishonestly if enough money was offered.
questions.promptZh: 那名商人認為，只要有人出足夠的錢，任何人都可以被說服做不誠實的事。
questions.answer: The businessman believed that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 那名商人相信，只要出價夠高，任何人都可以被收買。

questions.prompt: The gang leader said that nobody would stay loyal if the reward became large enough.
questions.promptZh: 那名幫派首領說，只要報酬夠高，沒有人會一直保持忠誠。
questions.answer: The gang leader said that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 那名幫派首領說，人人都有價碼。

questions.prompt: According to the reporter, the politician thought that any person could be bought.
questions.promptZh: 據記者所說，那名政治人物認為任何人都可以被收買。
questions.answer: According to the reporter, the politician believed that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 據記者所說，那名政治人物相信人人都有價碼。

questions.prompt: The shop owner thought even honest inspectors would change their minds for enough money. He trusted money more than principles.
questions.promptZh: 店主認為，只要金額足夠，就連誠實的檢查員也會改變主意。他相信金錢多於原則。
questions.answer: The shop owner believed that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 那名店主相信，只要金額足夠，任何人都可能放棄原則。

questions.prompt: Liam said that anyone’s loyalty could be bought with the right offer.
questions.promptZh: 利亞姆說，只要條件合適，任何人的忠誠都可以被收買。
questions.answer: Liam said that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 利亞姆說，每個人都有可以被收買的價碼。

questions.prompt: The film presents a dark idea: no person’s principles are completely safe from money.
questions.promptZh: 這齣電影提出一個陰暗的想法：沒有人的原則能完全不受金錢影響。
questions.answer: The film presents the dark idea that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 這齣電影提出「人人都有價碼」這個陰暗想法。

questions.prompt: Some people think everyone has a point at which money becomes more important than honesty.
questions.promptZh: 有些人認為，每個人都有一個金錢會變得比誠實更重要的臨界點。
questions.answer: Some people think that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 有些人認為，只要利益夠大，任何人都可能動搖。

questions.prompt: The dishonest coach was sure he could buy anyone’s support. He only needed to offer enough.
questions.promptZh: 那名不誠實的教練肯定自己可以收買任何人的支持；他只需要提出足夠高的條件。
questions.answer: The dishonest coach was sure that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 那名不誠實的教練深信人人都有價碼。

questions.prompt: “Offer him more,” the dealer said. “Anyone can be bought.”
questions.promptZh: 「再多給他一點吧，」那名商人說。「任何人都可以被收買。」
questions.answer: “Every man has his price,” the dealer said.
questions.answerZh: 「人人都有價碼，」那名商人說。

questions.prompt: The novel’s villain believes that enough money can make any person betray their values.
questions.promptZh: 小說中的反派相信，只要金額足夠，任何人都會背棄自己的價值觀。
questions.answer: The novel’s villain believes that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 小說中的反派相信人人都有價碼。

questions.prompt: At first, Nora thought everyone could be bribed if the offer was high enough.
questions.promptZh: 最初，諾拉認為只要出價夠高，任何人都可以被賄賂。
questions.answer: At first, Nora believed that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 最初，諾拉相信人人都有價碼。

questions.prompt: The boss does not accept a final refusal. He still thinks nobody is completely beyond the reach of money.
questions.promptZh: 老闆不接受最後的拒絕。他仍然認為沒有人能完全不受金錢影響。
questions.answer: The boss still thinks that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 老闆仍然認為每個人都有可以被收買的價碼。

questions.prompt: The speaker will argue that all people can be bought if the offer is large enough.
questions.promptZh: 那名講者將會主張，只要出價夠高，所有人都可以被收買。
questions.answer: The speaker will argue that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 那名講者將會主張人人都有價碼。

questions.prompt: The detective has seen many people accept bribes. He has always believed that nobody is completely safe from temptation.
questions.promptZh: 那名偵探見過很多人收受賄賂；他一直相信沒有人能完全抵抗誘惑。
questions.answer: The detective has always believed that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 那名偵探一直相信，只要誘惑夠大，任何人都可能動搖。

questions.prompt: A: Why does Victor keep raising the offer? B: He thinks anyone will agree when enough money is offered.
questions.promptZh: 甲：為甚麼維克托不斷提高出價？乙：他認為只要金額足夠，任何人都會答應。
questions.answer: He thinks that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 他認為人人都有價碼。

questions.prompt: Does Marcus really believe that anyone can be bought?
questions.promptZh: 馬庫斯真的相信任何人都可以被收買嗎？
questions.answer: Does Marcus really believe that every man has his price?
questions.answerZh: 馬庫斯真的相信人人都有價碼嗎？

questions.prompt: People often repeat a cynical saying which claims that everyone can be bribed.
questions.promptZh: 人們經常重複一句很悲觀的說法，聲稱所有人都可以被賄賂。
questions.answer: People often say that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 人們經常說人人都有價碼。

questions.prompt: Grace refuses to accept the claim that everyone can be bought.
questions.promptZh: 格蕾絲拒絕接受「所有人都可以被收買」這個說法。
questions.answer: Grace refuses to believe that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 格蕾絲拒絕相信人人都有價碼。

questions.prompt: The lawyer knew money could influence many people, but he rejected the idea that it could influence everyone.
questions.promptZh: 那名律師知道金錢可以影響很多人，但他不接受金錢可以影響所有人的想法。
questions.answer: The lawyer knew money could influence many people, but he rejected the idea that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 那名律師知道金錢可以影響很多人，但他不接受「人人都有價碼」這個想法。

questions.prompt: A: The agent says the judge will agree if we offer enough. B: That is a terrible belief about people.
questions.promptZh: 甲：那名代理人說，只要我們出價夠高，法官便會答應。乙：這種看法實在把人想得太差。
questions.answer: The agent seems to believe that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 那名代理人似乎相信人人都有價碼。

questions.prompt: A: Why did the criminal offer the guard more and more money? B: He thought everyone had an amount they would accept.
questions.promptZh: 甲：為甚麼那名罪犯向守衛提出愈來愈高的金額？乙：他認為每個人都有一個會接受的價碼。
questions.answer: He thought that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 他認為每個人都有一個會接受的價碼。

questions.prompt: A wealthy buyer kept increasing his offer. He believed even a loyal worker could be persuaded to betray the company.
questions.promptZh: 一名富有的買家不斷提高出價。他相信就連忠誠的員工也可以被說服背叛公司。
questions.answer: The wealthy buyer acted as if every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 那名富有的買家行事時，彷彿相信人人都有價碼。

questions.prompt: The character laughs at honesty and says that a large enough reward can break anyone’s principles.
questions.promptZh: 那個角色嘲笑誠實，並說只要報酬夠高，任何人的原則都會被打破。
questions.answer: The character laughs at honesty because he believes that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 那個角色嘲笑誠實，因為他相信人人都有價碼。

questions.prompt: Why does the businessman never accept a final no? He believes a better offer will change anyone’s answer.
questions.promptZh: 為甚麼那名商人從不接受最後的拒絕？他相信提出更好的條件便能改變任何人的答案。
questions.answer: The businessman never accepts a final no because he believes that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 那名商人從不接受最後的拒絕，因為他相信人人都有價碼。

questions.prompt: A: I would never sell my friend’s secret. B: The villain says you would if the offer were high enough.
questions.promptZh: 甲：我絕不會出賣朋友的秘密。乙：那個反派說，只要出價夠高，你便會這樣做。
questions.answer: The villain believes that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 那個反派相信，只要出價夠高，任何人都可能被收買。

questions.prompt: Ethan offered the nurse money, but she reported him at once. His belief that anyone could be bought was clearly wrong.
questions.promptZh: 伊森向護士提出金錢，但她立即舉報了他。他那種「任何人都可以被收買」的想法明顯是錯的。
questions.answer: Ethan believed that every man has his price, but the nurse proved him wrong.
questions.answerZh: 伊森相信人人都有價碼，但那名護士證明他錯了。

questions.prompt: The officer turned down every offer. This challenges the cynical idea that everybody can be bribed.
questions.promptZh: 那名人員拒絕了所有出價。這件事挑戰了「所有人都可以被賄賂」這個悲觀想法。
questions.answer: The officer’s refusal challenges the idea that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 那名人員的拒絕挑戰了「人人都有價碼」這個想法。

questions.prompt: The play asks a difficult question: can every person be persuaded to betray their values for the right reward?
questions.promptZh: 這齣戲提出一個難題：只要報酬合適，每個人都會被說服背棄自己的價值觀嗎？
questions.answer: The play asks whether every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 這齣戲探問是否每個人都有可以被收買的價碼。

questions.prompt: A: Do you think Daniel will betray us for money? B: No. I do not accept the idea that everyone can be bought.
questions.promptZh: 甲：你認為丹尼爾會為了錢背叛我們嗎？乙：不。我不接受所有人都可以被收買這個想法。
questions.answer: No. I do not believe that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 不。我不相信人人都有價碼。

questions.prompt: The article warns that believing everyone can be bought may lead powerful people to treat others badly.
questions.promptZh: 文章警告，若相信所有人都可以被收買，掌權者可能會惡劣地對待他人。
questions.answer: The article warns against believing that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 文章提醒人們不要相信人人都有價碼。

questions.prompt: Although the mayor had seen many cases of bribery, she still refused to believe that all people could be bought.
questions.promptZh: 雖然市長見過很多賄賂個案，她仍然拒絕相信所有人都可以被收買。
questions.answer: Although the mayor had seen many cases of bribery, she still refused to believe that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 雖然市長見過很多賄賂個案，她仍然拒絕相信人人都有價碼。

questions.prompt: The gang kept making larger offers because its leader believed nobody would remain honest forever.
questions.promptZh: 那個幫派不斷提高出價，因為首領相信沒有人會永遠保持誠實。
questions.answer: The gang kept making larger offers because its leader believed that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 那個幫派不斷提高出價，因為首領相信人人都有價碼。

questions.prompt: A: Why are they offering the witness a house now? B: Their leader thinks everybody has an amount they will accept.
questions.promptZh: 甲：為甚麼他們現在向證人提出送一所房子？乙：他們的首領認為每個人都有一個會接受的價碼。
questions.answer: Their leader seems to think that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 他們的首領似乎認為每個人都有一個會接受的價碼。

questions.prompt: Most of the team trusted people’s principles, but Colin believed anyone could be bought.
questions.promptZh: 團隊大部分成員都相信人的原則，但科林認為任何人都可以被收買。
questions.answer: Most of the team trusted people’s principles, but Colin believed that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 團隊大部分成員都相信人的原則，但科林相信人人都有價碼。

questions.prompt: The first two officials refused the bribe. The businessman did not stop, because he thought a higher amount would eventually work.
questions.promptZh: 首兩名官員拒絕了賄賂。那名商人沒有停手，因為他認為更高的金額最終會奏效。
questions.answer: Even after two officials refused the bribe, the businessman still believed that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 即使已有兩名官員拒絕賄賂，那名商人仍然相信人人都有價碼。

questions.prompt: The documentary does not say that everyone can be bought. It asks whether enough money can overcome anyone’s principles.
questions.promptZh: 這齣紀錄片沒有說所有人都可以被收買；它探問足夠的金錢是否能勝過任何人的原則。
questions.answer: The documentary does not claim that every man has his price; it asks whether the proverb is true.
questions.answerZh: 這齣紀錄片沒有斷言人人都有價碼；它只是探問這句諺語是否成立。

questions.prompt: A: Martin says the guard will agree when the offer reaches NT$50,000. B: Martin has a very low opinion of human honesty.
questions.promptZh: 甲：馬丁說，當出價達到新台幣五萬元時，守衛便會答應。乙：馬丁對人的誠信看得很低。
questions.answer: Martin clearly believes that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 馬丁顯然相信，只要出價夠高，任何人都可以被收買。

questions.prompt: The dealer smiled and said that anyone could be bought if the offer was high enough.
questions.promptZh: 那名商人笑着說，只要出價夠高，任何人都可以被收買。
questions.answer: “Every man has his price,” the dealer said with a smile.
questions.answerZh: 「人人都有價碼，」那名商人笑着說。

questions.prompt: If the director truly thinks no employee will stay loyal when enough money is offered, he has a very negative view of people.
questions.promptZh: 如果那名主管真的認為，只要有人出足夠的錢，沒有員工會保持忠誠，那麼他對人的看法便十分負面。
questions.answer: If the director truly believes that every man has his price, he has a very negative view of people.
questions.answerZh: 如果那名主管真的相信人人都有價碼，那麼他對人的看法便十分負面。

questions.prompt: A: You think I will betray my team for more money. B: I admit that I believe everyone has an amount that will make them change their mind.
questions.promptZh: 甲：你認為我會為了更多錢背叛團隊。乙：我承認，我相信每個人都有一個會使自己動搖的價碼。
questions.answer: I admit that I believe every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 我承認，我相信人人都有價碼。

questions.prompt: A lesson about bribes shows a dishonest business owner offering larger and larger payments because he assumes everyone can be bought.
questions.promptZh: 一課有關賄賂的教材描述一名不誠實的店主不斷提高金額，因為他假定所有人都可以被收買。
questions.answer: The lesson presents a business owner who believes that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 這課教材描述一名相信人人都有價碼的店主。

questions.prompt: The detective notices that the criminal never asks whether people are honest; he only asks how much money they want.
questions.promptZh: 那名偵探留意到，罪犯從不問別人是否誠實，只問他們想要多少錢。
questions.answer: The detective realises that the criminal believes that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 那名偵探明白到，罪犯相信人人都有價碼。

questions.prompt: The repeated offers reveal a belief that no person’s loyalty is beyond money.
questions.promptZh: 一次又一次的出價顯示，有人相信沒有人的忠誠能超越金錢。
questions.answer: The repeated offers reveal the belief that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 一次又一次的出價顯示出「人人都有價碼」這個信念。

questions.prompt: A: The manager says the worker’s first refusal means nothing. B: Why? A: He thinks a bigger reward will change the answer.
questions.promptZh: 甲：經理說，那名員工第一次拒絕並不代表甚麼。乙：為甚麼？甲：他認為更大的報酬會改變答案。
questions.answer: The manager is acting on the belief that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 那名經理正按照「人人都有價碼」這個信念行事。

questions.prompt: The judge said that many people can be tempted, but it is wrong to claim that everyone can be bought.
questions.promptZh: 法官說，很多人可能會受到誘惑，但聲稱所有人都可以被收買是錯誤的。
questions.answer: The judge accepted that many people can be tempted but rejected the claim that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 法官承認很多人可能會受到誘惑，但拒絕接受「人人都有價碼」這個說法。

questions.prompt: In the novel, the villain measures loyalty only in money and never accepts that a person may refuse every offer.
questions.promptZh: 在小說中，反派只用金錢衡量忠誠，從不接受有人可能拒絕所有出價。
questions.answer: In the novel, the villain acts on the belief that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 在小說中，反派按照「人人都有價碼」這個信念行事。

questions.prompt: A: Why did she tear up the cheque? B: She wanted to show that her honesty was not for sale.
questions.promptZh: 甲：她為甚麼撕掉支票？乙：她想表明自己的誠信不是用來出售的。
questions.answer: She tore up the cheque to show that the saying “every man has his price” is not always true.
questions.answerZh: 她撕掉支票，以表明「人人都有價碼」這句話並非總是正確。

questions.prompt: The story suggests, rather than proves, that nobody may be completely safe from a large enough reward.
questions.promptZh: 這個故事只是暗示，而不是證明，沒有人能完全抵抗足夠大的報酬。
questions.answer: The story suggests that every man has his price, but it does not present this as a proven fact.
questions.answerZh: 這個故事暗示人人都有價碼，但沒有把這個觀點說成已證實的事實。

questions.prompt: The businessman failed to buy the teacher’s silence. The final scene therefore questions his belief that no one is beyond bribery.
questions.promptZh: 那名商人未能用金錢換取老師保持沉默。因此，最後一幕質疑了他那種「沒有人不能被賄賂」的信念。
questions.answer: By showing the teacher refusing the money, the final scene questions the belief that every man has his price.
questions.answerZh: 最後一幕透過呈現老師拒絕金錢，質疑了「人人都有價碼」這個信念。

questions.prompt: A company director keeps offering a worker more money to hide a serious safety problem. The worker refuses and reports it, showing that the director’s negative view of people is not always correct.
questions.promptZh: 一名公司主管不斷向員工提出更多金錢，要求他隱瞞嚴重的安全問題。員工拒絕並作出舉報，顯示主管對人性的負面看法並非總是正確。
questions.answer: Although the director believes that every man has his price, the worker’s refusal shows that this negative view is not always correct.
questions.answerZh: 雖然那名主管相信人人都有價碼，但員工的拒絕顯示這種負面看法並非總是正確。
